name: five-orites-scoop
description: Five-orites Scoop — Premium Ice Cream E-Commerce + Real-Time Inventory App

scripts.test: npm run test:logic && npm run test:rules
scripts.build:android: ng build && npx cap sync android && npx cap open android
scripts.build:ios: ng build && npx cap sync ios && npx cap open ios
scripts.seed:preserve-stock: cross-env PRESERVE_STOCK=true npx ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/seed-products.ts
scripts.images:seed: cross-env IMAGE_FROM_ASSETS=true npx ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/seed-products.ts
scripts.deploy: npm run deploy:firestore && npm run deploy:functions && npm run deploy:hosting
scripts.deploy:hosting: npm run build && firebase deploy --only hosting
scripts.deploy:functions: npm --prefix functions run build && firebase deploy --only functions
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:scripts && npm run test:logic && npm run test:rules && npm run check:contrast && npm run build

//engines: Angular 17 is built and tested against Node 18.13.x / 20.9.x (see .nvmrc = 20). Its `engines` field is a floor, not a ceiling, so npm silently accepts Node 22/24 and you get failures with no diagnostic pointing at the version. This upper bound fails fast instead. `node -v` before blaming the build.
//overrides: @angular/fire@17 declares an OPTIONAL peer on firebase-tools@^13, but this project needs firebase-tools 15 for `firebase emulators:exec` (the v1 Firestore emulator it ships). Without this override every `npm install` dies with ERESOLVE. The peer is genuinely optional — it is only used by `ng add @angular/fire` when scaffolding emulators, which this project configures by hand in firebase.json.
